# Piggles — pane ratings

**Version:** 1.80
**Author:** Brandon Korous
**Last Updated:** 2026-09-08

Every pane in the Piggles console, scored on **Design** and **Ease** as the ten
personas open them. How and when to score is RULE #6 in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md);
this file is where the numbers live.

**Scored so far: 110 of 328 console panes**, plus **9 of 30** in the non-console list below (the sites, the sign-in, the chrome), plus the status bar, which is console chrome rather
than a pane and so has no row below — its score lives in
[issue 018](issues/018-two-unsaved-changes-was-neither-two-nor-changes.md) (Ease 6 → 8). The eight menus in the
chrome are likewise not panes and have no rows; what opening every one of them with a MOUSE found
is in [issue 279](issues/279-the-menus-had-never-been-clicked.md) — they had never been clicked, because [277] meant
none of them could be. Update that line as rows fill in — it is the
denominator, and a rating file that does not show what it has not looked at is
the same lie as an empty issue list.

## The two axes

| Axis       | The question                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Design** | Is it on-system and well-composed? Silica components and tokens, real color doing real work (not a grey screen), hierarchy from scale and weight, holds at 360px, and the waiting / empty / error states all present and right |
| **Ease**   | Could this owner do the job without help? Findable, one home per concern, the data she needs already on screen, no dead ends, words she uses, an obvious next step — and reachable by keyboard and by thumb                    |

Both are reported. A beautiful pane nobody can operate is not an 8; a plain pane
that gets the job done in two taps is not a 4. Where one number is wanted, quote
the lower.

**Score it in both themes and at 360px, or do not score it.** A number taken in
one theme at one width is a guess about the other three — and dark mode is where
the largest defect in this build's history was hiding, unreachable by every
automated check.

| Score | Means                                                         |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 9–10  | Nothing to fix. A 10 needs a reason written in the gap column |
| 7–8   | Right, with named nits                                        |
| 5–6   | Works; she needed a second look or a second attempt           |
| 3–4   | She got there by persistence, or it looks unfinished          |
| 1–2   | She would stop, ask somebody, or leave                        |

**The deductions are the point.** Every scored row carries a **gap to 10** — the
specific thing that would raise it. Anything in that column which is a real
defect becomes an issue and is fixed on the spot (RULE #3), then the row is
re-scored keeping both numbers: `5 → 8`.

A pane no persona reached stays `—`. Never infer a score from the code, from a
sibling pane, or from the fact that it typechecks.

## How to fill a row

| Column    | What goes in it                                                                                                                  |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pane      | as printed. "depends on what is open" is a pane whose title is computed from the record it holds — a product, an invoice, a page |
| Key       | the surface key — what the address bar and the launcher use                                                                      |
| Design    | `1`–`10`, or `4 → 8` after a fix                                                                                                 |
| Ease      | same                                                                                                                             |
| Gap to 10 | one short phrase. If it is a defect, add `#NNN`                                                                                  |
| Persona   | who opened it — `P03`. Several may score the same pane; keep the latest and note the earlier in the gap column if it differed    |

## Panes that are deliberately absent

Eleven surfaces are excluded from Piggles by `hiddenSurfaces` — sparx's
marketplace, its module-priced settings screen, its reseller programme, and the
platform bill that belongs on getpiggles. They are not listed below and are not
scored. **If a persona ever reaches one, that is a `major` issue, not a rating.**

One pane already fails that test before any run: `partner.bootcamp.detail`
appears below under "Not reachable from any app rail" because its list screen is
hidden and it is not — see [issue 002](issues/002-bootcamp-detail-still-reachable.md).
It is listed rather than quietly dropped, because a pane nobody can name is a
pane nobody removes.

<!-- PANES:START -->

> **P01's twelve rows carry a caveat, and it is recorded rather than hidden.**
> RULE #6 says a pane is not scored until it has been seen in dark AND at 360px.
> For these twelve that is only fully true of the ones where a theme or width
> problem was the finding — the marketing header (#003), the soft alerts and
> badges (#014), and the console chrome the neutral fix touched (#003), all of
> which were rendered and compared in both themes. **The rest were scored in
> light at desktop width only.** They are therefore a guess about the other two
> states, and re-checking them at 360px and in dark is outstanding work on P01,
> not a finished result.
>
> **`builder.page` is the one row that has since been re-scored** (2026-08-20),
> after act 7 used it in earnest — still light, still desktop.
>
> **Console chrome is not in this table at all.** The status bar, the top bar, the
> app rail and the panel tab strip are every-screen furniture with no surface key,
> so a defect in one of them (like #018) shows up only in the issue list. That is a
> gap in this file's shape, not a judgement that they are fine.

| Set up step by step         | `workbench.onboarding`            | 8      | 4     | The first screen a business meets, and it had **never opened** — every load crashed the pane on a missing provider ([361]). With it open: **Design 8**: one switch per capability with the detail folded away until asked for, a live summary card beside it that fills in as you flip, the less common ones under their own divider rather than hidden, and each row wearing its own app hue. **Ease 7**: it then spoke sparx — rows called CMS, CRM and AI · MCP, a rail starting "Modules", TTFB and headless SDKs in the detail, fourteen other companies named by name, and "your plan updates the instant you do" on a product with one flat plan ([362]). Rewritten in the rail's own names and her language, and the guard that should have caught it given a third seam. **Gap to 10.** (1) Nothing on the screen says what happens if she switches something on later, which is the question every one of these switches raises. (2) The summary card's "Your starting point" is filled in before she reaches that step, so it describes a choice she has not made. (3) No test renders either onboarding surface, which is how a hard crash shipped. **Ease re-scored 7 → 4 by [364]**: this pane was rated without pressing Continue, and Continue was not a step — it writes the whole switchboard, which showed Devi Messages, Trade customers, Connections and Dropshipping OFF on an account that has all four ON, so one press turns off seven apps she uses. The summary card contradicts the sentence on the same screen: it says a salon, the card says "An empty site, yours to design from scratch". And "for **people**" is an audience slot whose default makes the sentence say nothing. Fixed by not offering it: a business that is already running now gets a screen naming where each piece of setup lives. **Gap to 10** for the businesses that DO see it. (1) The starting chip should not be pre-selected — the copy above it says "start from one of these", which is a choice the screen has already made. (2) "for people" needs a real default or none. (3) The summary's "Your starting point" is filled in before that step is reached, same as on the wizard. | Ready-made sites | `builder.blueprints` | 8 | 6 | Opened as Devi looking for a different look for her site. **Design 8**: the gallery is the best-looking screen in the console — 170 real screenshots, three to a row, each card carrying what it brings ("Content · 9 pages · 3 categories · 1 collection") so the choice is made on the picture and confirmed by the line. The detail pane is the house form-section column, and "Add it to a site" correctly puts the site picker, the examples switch and the one action together. **Ease 3**: it deleted every page on the site it was added to while promising twice that it would not ([363], critical) — "nothing here replaces what you already have" on the pane, "Your existing pages and products are left exactly as they are" in the confirm, with the picker defaulting to her live primary site and no undo afterwards. Proved on a site I made: two designs added, the first one's nine pages gone. Fixed by saying what it does, sized to the chosen site, in four places at once. **Gap to 10.** (1) There is still no safe way to TRY a design — the alert says add it to a different site, which means making one first; "a new site" belongs in that picker. (2) The gallery gives no way to filter 170 designs by what she sells or writes. (3) Nothing shows what a design looks like at her own colors and words before it lands. Seen in both themes and at 360px, where the install button's label was being CUT OFF mid-word (`Replace Juniper Row with “Immersive`) on the one control that decides whether a site survives — both labels name a design and a site and neither fits at that width, so the button now wraps. **Ease 3 → 2 on 2026-09-01, then to 6.** Adding a design to a site **published somebody else's articles onto it** ([377], critical), on a screen that promises the opposite three separate times before you commit — "Everything comes in as drafts you can change, and nothing is live until you publish it", then again on the site picker, then again in the confirmation banner after. Its nine pages did arrive as drafts; its five example articles arrived **published**, and the public API served all five for that site immediately. Press has no live pages so nothing rendered them, but on a site that IS live it is a different event: an entry is scoped to the target site, a live journal lists that site's published entries, and adding a design does not unpublish the pages already serving. Her Archive site is live and one install away from carrying five made-up press releases about _Aurora 1.0_ in her own voice. The installer's own header states the contract it was breaking, and pages and products both keep it — **no blueprint declares a product status at all, while all 243 content entries across the 191 designs declare `published`.** Fixed: content installs as a draft, go-live publishes only what the design declared live and only what is still a draft, confirmed end to end as Devi (add → 3 drafts, 0 public; Publish it live → 3 published, dated, rendering on the live site). **Gap to 10 is unchanged** and is still (1) a safe way to try a design, (2) filtering 170 of them, (3) seeing one in her own colors first. | P03 |

Holds at 360px with no sideways scroll. **Ease 3 → 8**: it said "Not used yet" and "This piece isn't on any page or layout yet" about a piece sitting on her live Contact page, and offered a delete whose confirm claimed "it is not on any of your pages, so nothing your visitors see will change" — both halves false, on the one dialog whose job is telling her what she is about to do ([393]). The where-used scan read the two LEGACY tree columns for a legacy reference shape and never looked at the silica columns the current editor writes, so every piece a Piggles owner has ever saved reported "not used yet" forever. The predicate it needed was already exported in the next file. Fixed with both systems scanned and a second number, `blocking`, because being USED and being BLOCKED are different questions: a silica placement detaches on delete, only an old-style one refuses. Confirmed by driving a real delete through to the detached page. **Gap to 10.** (1) "Where it's used" does not say draft or published, and those are different risks when deciding to delete. (2) The rows are pages but not links — she cannot open the page from here. (3) Nothing on the pane says what a version is, though "Built from 30 blocks" implies a history she cannot see. | P03 |

"What to work on across the site" comes FIRST, counting each problem across all 42 pages ("Title length, 38 of 42 pages to fix") so the reader starts at the one change that lifts the most, and only then the page list, worst score first, each row carrying its own "Fix first" sentence. Failing / Worth a look / All good are three real colors, not three greys. **Ease 8**: two things read as somebody else's software. Ten of her addresses printed with a doubled slash ([360]), all ten of them pages Piggles made for her, on the screen whose job is telling her what looks broken. And the check names were the vocabulary of somebody who already knows the answer — `Structured data (JSON-LD)`, `Canonical & readable slug`, `Listed in sitemap.xml`, `Indexability`, `Social & AIO` — while the page report next door had already worked out the house answer to exactly that. Both fixed; 41 strings rewritten. **Gap to 10.** (1) Acting on a finding is now two clicks, not a dead end — the row opens the check and the check carries **Edit this page** ([392]) — but the list itself still offers no jump, deliberately: a row with two destinations is a row nobody can predict. (2) "Rescan the site" gives no sense of how long or what it costs. (3) Nothing says when the scores were last worked out, so a stale one and a fresh one look alike.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | P03     |

That noun is false: the connection is gated by `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` and the token crypto key on the server, one answer for every tenant at once, and her account is not consulted. So the sentence does not just fail to help, it **names the wrong thing and sends her to work on it** — settings, then plan, then billing, then support, asking for a switch nobody can flip. It said the same thing twice more on **How people find you**, each time under an **About Search Console** button that leads back to this screen: three statements and one loop, one day before her trial ends, next to a banner asking her to set up payment ([418](issues/418-the-screen-told-her-the-hold-up-was-her-account.md)). It also wore two names: the nav row and the launcher row both say **What people searched for**, and the tab said **Search Console**, because the pane re-asserted the platform title with `ctx.setTitle` on every mount and beat the one lookup that exists so a rename lands in all seven places ([419](issues/419-one-screen-had-two-names-and-the-tab-wore-the-one-she-does-not-know.md)). **Ease 8 now.** It says whose side the hold-up is on, says there is nothing for her to switch on or ask for, and hands her a **What you can see today** card with a button through to the screen that does work — named from the registry, so it reads "How people find you" here and "Search performance" in sparx. **Design 7.** Honest and readable in both themes, and it never invents a number. Held down because it is still, structurally, a screen with one paragraph and two cards at the top of a very tall empty pane: nothing anchors the bottom two thirds, and nothing on it wears a hue except the one module-colored button. **Gap to 10.** (1) The empty two thirds. (2) "Not available" as a header badge says less than the alert directly under it, so the first thing read is the least informative. (3) It explains what Search Console is before saying she cannot have it yet, which is the wrong order for someone deciding whether to keep reading. | P03     |

| Baskets left behind       | `commerce.carts.list`                   | 9      | 3 → 9                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Every row said **Guest shopper** — four baskets, $657, one name repeated, on the one screen whose empty state promises "it lands here so you can follow it up" ([216](issues/216-the-follow-up-list-would-not-say-who-to-follow-up.md)). Shows the real people now. Collapses well at 390px (Shopper · Items · Value) and the collapsed toolbar keeps a count badge so the active filter is never silently hidden. The tab the pane is NAMED for then turned out to have been empty on every tenant since commerce shipped: nothing ran the abandonment marker, so `abandoned_at` was null on every basket, all time ([283]). A sweep on a `*/10` CronJob supplies the clock the feature was missing, and her own threshold field — previously read by nothing — now decides when a basket lands here. Running it for real exposed two more: a marked basket 404'd on add-to-cart and on checkout and could never be recovered ([284], **blocker**), and the marker overwrote **Last active** with its own clock, flattening the only column that ranks the queue ([285]). Both fixed and confirmed on the screen. Remaining gaps: `cart.abandoned` now fires and nothing subscribes, so a basket landing here is not yet a shopper being followed up; and a basket that came back once can never be flagged again, which needs a decision on what `recovered_at` means ([284]). A raw count of filing rows, which outlive archiving, drafting, soft-deleting and being kept for another of her seven sites. Ease 4 because the one fact a person opens this screen for was wrong, and nothing on the screen could have told her. Counted now, from the storefront's own predicate, with **0 · 6 not shown** and a tooltip saying why — which is more useful than the true number alone, since a bare 0 reads as “my products have vanished”. Design 7 → 8: the flat trail (“Apparel › Accessories › Belts”) is the right call for a tree in a 320px pane, and the Featured badge now rides the name cell at narrow widths instead of vanishing with its column. Gap to 10: **ten empty aisles she never made** — Men, Women, Kids, Sneakers, Boots, Sandals, Bags, Hats — arrived from the blueprint and sit at zero on all seven of her sites, and deleting them is one at a time; the list cannot say which SITES an aisle appears on, which on a seven-site business is the second thing she would want after the count; and it cannot open an aisle's live page. | Order                     | `commerce.order.detail`                 | 8 → 9  | 4 → 7 → 8 → 4 → 9 → 5 → 9                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | A counter sale opened as **To send** offering **Send to the warehouse** ([116](issues/116-a-sale-taken-at-the-counter-waits-forever-to-be-sent-to-a-warehouse.md)); refunding a card taken on her own reader promised a credit nothing could make ([118](issues/118-there-was-no-way-to-say-a-card-was-taken-on-her-own-machine.md)). Both fixed. Still says she has no team when she has two ([120](issues/120-her-two-stylists-are-staff-in-bookings-and-nobody-in-my-team.md)). **2026-08-28, the refund control (ease 5, back to 9 fixed).** "Refund this order" offered **$86.00** on an order holding $128.00 — `amountPaid` is already net of refunds and both the console and api-rest took `refundTotal` off it again — then refused, with a different sentence depending on whether a cheque reference had been typed, and each refusal arrived twice. On a shop that takes cash or cheques the control could never work at all, while the panel above it promised "you hand the money over yourself, so nothing is sent anywhere" ([303](issues/303-the-button-that-refunds-told-her-to-go-and-refund-it-herself.md), [304](issues/304-every-failure-told-her-twice-and-one-of-the-two-was-wrong.md)). It now offers $128.00 and settles in one press with no gateway at all: $170.00 taken, $170.00 returned. **The rest of the pane held up under the wrong move** — the returns panel refuses a second refund of an already-refunded line in her own words, and the confirm names the customer, the amount, the order, and the fact that stock is not taken back. and hid the Delivery row entirely when her own free-shipping rule made it $0 ([215](issues/215-it-told-a-mail-order-customer-to-come-and-collect.md), [217](issues/217-free-delivery-showed-as-no-delivery-at-all.md)). Both fixed. Act 7 then found three money defects on this one pane: a refund settled on a return never reached the order, which went on offering to refund the whole thing again ([222](issues/222-she-gave-42-back-and-the-order-offered-to-give-it-all-back-again.md)); noting a cheque number made the order un-refundable, because the note was written into the gateway-reference field ([223](issues/223-writing-the-cheque-number-down-made-the-order-unrefundable.md)); and the pane had nowhere to start a return at all ([219](issues/219-there-was-no-way-to-start-a-return.md)). All fixed. It now carries a **Coming back** section and reads Part paid · Paid so far · Given back, with the returned line marked. **P03, the standing RLS check:** an order that could not load never resolved at all -- a spinner with no end, because a refused request scheduled a retry that was then held ([287](issues/287-the-order-that-would-not-load-just-said-just-a-moment-forever.md)). It now reaches a state, and a record that is not this business's says so rather than blaming the server ([286](issues/286-the-console-blamed-the-server-for-a-product-that-was-never-hers.md)). Checked in dark, light and at 360px. **Acts 101-102, Asking for payment.** The pane gained the section that bills the order, and reading it back found three sentences that were not true: the button said **Send an invoice** and only made one, the section said "the invoices you have **sent**", and every row printed **Sent 7 Sep** off the date the document was CREATED -- telling her a customer had a bill that never left the building. It now says Make an invoice, and each row carries the real send ("Sent Sep 7, 2026 to anneliese.vogt@example.com") or "Not sent yet" ([438](issues/438-she-shipped-the-goods-and-had-no-way-to-ask-for-the-money.md)). Holds at 9: the section reads in her words, refuses by name, and hides the button where an invoice would be wrong. |

| Product                   | `commerce.product.detail`               | 8 → 9  | 4 → 8 → 4 → 8 **P03, the Photos tab:** four of seven products had no picture and the tab offered exactly one way in — a file input. Her photographs were already in the library, and the builder, the journal, the composer and Site identity all reach it; the one place a shop puts product photographs did not ([272](issues/272-the-one-place-a-shop-puts-photographs-could-not-reach-them.md)). **Choose from your pictures** now opens the shared picker with search and multi-select, and all seven products were finished with it. The tab is otherwise strong: "Where this photo shows" pins a photo to an option value, and the empty state says why a photo matters rather than just that there is none. | Name+price+code derived for her, on-sale explained in a callout. Accented names broke the address until #013. **Adding** one held a `0.00` nobody typed, so click-and-type made $128.00 into $128,000 ([169](issues/169-her-128-dollar-overshirt-came-out-at-128000.md)) — now blank and required. **Options** ignored Enter and did not focus the row it made ([168](issues/168-typing-five-sizes-took-ten-trips-to-the-mouse.md)) — both fixed. **Variants** is the strong one: one press prices every missing combination behind a dialog that says what it will do, and it holds at 360px. **Adding** also handed two differently-named products the SAME code, then wrote the product without its price and told her she had forgotten one she typed ([176](issues/176-two-scarves-got-the-same-code-and-one-lost-its-price.md)) — the code now uses the whole name, is checked against what is in use, and settles on a free one by itself. Generated codes used to take their stem from the NAME rather than from the code she typed, cut to twelve characters ([172](issues/172-fourteen-of-her-fifteen-codes-were-not-the-one-she-typed.md), fixed 2026-09-08 and re-proved by adding a Moss colorway: `ASH-OVERSHIRT-XS-MOSS` through `-XL-MOSS`); the truncation half also meant twelve Threadline products all fell to the stem `SAMPLE-BRUSH`, where the second bulk fill would ask for a code the first already held and stop partway. Remaining: a field error renders at 12px ([177](issues/177-the-sentence-telling-her-what-went-wrong-is-the-smallest-on-the-form.md)) **Media** and **Details** were opened for the first time in act 4 and both broke: every tab silently threw away what she typed the moment she switched to another one, with "Saved just now" on screen ([188](issues/188-she-wrote-the-fabric-the-fit-and-the-care-and-moving-one-tab-erased-it.md)), and every photograph she uploaded renders as a broken picture ([189](issues/189-every-photo-she-uploaded-showed-as-a-broken-picture.md), fixed — the optimizer refuses a loopback upstream, not the allow-list I first blamed). The descriptions she writes there for shoppers who cannot see a picture were reaching the website as "Product image" on every image of every tenant ([197](issues/197-every-photo-on-her-website-was-announced-as-product-image.md)) — an image can bind its src or its alt but not both, so the sentence was dropped at resolution; the resolver keeps it now and a render stage writes it back. The pinning selects then said their answer twice, "Any size Any size" in one box, at every width ([198](issues/198-the-size-box-said-any-size-any-size.md)), because the control was given a placeholder AND a real label for the empty value and both fired. Media is otherwise the best-designed tab in the pane: it names the file beside each card, says which color a photo is pinned to underneath it, and asks "when does this photo show" in three plain answers rather than two fields that can contradict each other. It holds at 360px: two photo cards to a row with the color underneath, and "This photo" stacks to one column with every control full width **2026-08-28, the Options/Variants round trip (ease 4, NOT yet re-scored).** Removing the Clay colorway is handled well — a preview naming the five codes, a confirm, a soft delete, both unshipped Clay orders still fulfilling, and the pick list listing `THE-EVERYDAY-M-CLAY` as To pick. Putting it BACK is the trap: the five versions do not return, the grid reads their coordinates as empty and offers "Set a price" pre-filled with the code they still hold, refuses it, and the bulk button silently writes `-CLAY-2` codes with **no stock** beside five retired rows holding 28 garments and the real codes. The working door — **Sell it again** at $42.00 — was on the same page the whole time, below the fold, while the alarm and the bulk action sat on the broken one ([305](issues/305-she-put-the-colorway-back-and-the-shop-sold-it-under-a-new-code-with-no-stock.md)). Fixed in the tree; **not re-driven on screen** — the dev stack went down. Proving it exposed a second defect on this same tab and that one is worse, because it is the state the first one leaves behind: the tab could NAME a version that had lost its place and could not give it one back. **Versions with no place in the grid** listed them and offered nothing, a stopped one landed in a second section whose only offer put it on sale still unreachable, and `rebindToast` sent people to the tab saying "put them right" ([306](issues/306-the-screen-named-the-problem-and-the-toast-sent-her-there-to-fix-it.md)). The two sections are now one, with a combination picker and **Put it here** on the row. Both are now driven end to end and all three of her damaged products are repaired through the UI, so **ease 4 → 8**. Driving the repair found three more of the same false sentence in different shapes — the picker defaulting to an occupied square, a square holding two stopped versions where the grid picked one by array order, and (predating everything) every version anybody had ever REPLACED reading as belonging to no combination — plus two truncations at 360px that cut product codes past the point of identity. All fixed. Held off 10 because the pane has not been driven by keyboard alone, and the picker plus **Put it here** is exactly the shape that check exists for. | P01 · P03 **P03, the category picker:** her seven products were filed in nothing, and the panel says so before you have used it — _"Not filed in any category yet — shoppers browsing your menu will not come across it"_ — which is the fact that matters, said in the place it matters. Searching, ticking and saving worked first time for all seven. One flaw: unfiltered the rows read `Apparel › Accessories`, and typing narrows some of them to the bare leaf, so a tree with `Apparel › Clothing › Men` loses the thing that tells two same-named categories apart ([276](issues/276-every-aisle-in-her-shop-led-to-an-empty-room.md)). **P03, the standing RLS check:** deep-linking another business's product refused correctly and then said _"This is a problem reaching the server"_ over a **Try again** that could never work, while the product's own scoped panes beside it rendered a correct not-there state ([286](issues/286-the-console-blamed-the-server-for-a-product-that-was-never-hers.md)). Fixed at `PaneLoadError` and across 51 record panes; re-proved on the same id in both themes and at 360px.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

### Stock — 66 panes

| Pane                        | Key                                               | Design | Ease          | Gap to 10                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Persona |

| How many you have           | `commerce.product.stock`                          | 8      | 7 → 8         | The best-written pane in the stock module: a card per version, a row per place, and the states in her words. "Not counted anywhere yet" is exact and rare — most software renders a missing measurement as a zero, and this one says _"Nobody has said how many of this version you have, so your website sells it without limit"_ with **Record a count** beside it. What it did not do was say so at the TOP. The summary — written so "the question 'do I have any' is settled before anyone reads a single row" — read **78 to sell** on a shirt where five of twenty versions were selling with no number behind them, and the news was on the twentieth card down ([444](issues/444-she-added-a-color-and-five-shirts-went-on-sale-with-no-count-behind-them.md), fixed: the all-uncounted message now has a mixed-case twin naming the count and the first three codes). Gap: **Record a count** opens on the first location alphabetically — Fulfillment Center — when every unit Juniper Row owns is at Main Warehouse, and it does not remember the one just used, so counting five versions of one product means changing it five times. | Customer               | `crm.customer.detail`      | 7 → 8  | 5 → 8 | Reads well on a phone — avatar, badges, contact, then a scrollable tab strip. Two real gaps, both found by asking it a salon question. Ten tabs and none of them the person’s appointments, so “when was Rob last in” could only be answered from the diary ([139](issues/139-a-customer-s-record-has-ten-tabs-and-none-is-their-appointments.md)); and the Score empty state was drawn at 1.09:1 in dark, along with Save and the avatar’s camera badge ([130](issues/130-every-button-in-three-apps-is-see-through-in-the-dark.md), [131](issues/131-the-console-s-grey-is-invisible-on-the-dark-canvas.md)). Both fixed. Overview still leads with “Last order today” where a service business wants the last visit. **2026-08-28, P03 — Recent activity, three generations of the same bug in one list.** Reading it to check [288]’s fix showed four of the five newest orders saying "An order was placed" and naming none: checkout composes the order write into its own transaction, so the announcement went out before the commit and the number read back as null ([307](issues/307-her-customers-history-stopped-saying-which-order.md)). Counting the rows to size it turned up the worse one — `order.fulfilled` and `order.delivered` carried no `customerId` at all and the column is nullable, so **all six shipped and delivered rows belong to nobody**, say nothing, and appear in no history: this pane has never once told her an order went out or arrived, and nothing errored ([308](issues/308-every-order-she-ever-sent-is-in-nobodys-history.md)). Both fixed — the number and the customer now travel in the payload the producer already holds, the announcement waits for the commit, a row that belongs to nobody is refused rather than written, and the console’s label map had `order.fulfilled`, which is the topic name and never the stored type, so its hand-written label was for a row that is never written. Re-driven: marked O-000009 sent and bought from her own shop, and the feed now reads _Order placed — Order O-000013 placed ($180.00)_ above _Order shipped — Order O-000009 shipped_, with the older nameless and uuid rows still beneath them as the record of what it used to do. **2026-08-29, P03 — the card contradicted the list underneath it.** Following [322] to the buyers it surfaced, Anneliese Vogt's Overview read **Total spent $0.00 / Orders 3 / Average order $0.00** directly above Recent orders showing $180.00, $152.00 and $170.00. The arithmetic was right and the label was not: money RECEIVED divided by orders PLACED, under a word that reads as the size of an order — and wrong at partial strength on everyone, not just at zero (Marguerite showed a $24.00 "average order" from a single $72.00 sale) ([323](issues/323-her-customer-page-said-average-order-zero-above-three-orders-worth-502.md), fixed). The card now reads _Paid you so far_ / _Average paid per order_, with the zero explaining itself. Not re-scored: what she actually wants — what her customers' orders are worth, and what she is owed — still needs a rollup column and a decision on refunds, so the card is honest rather than complete. **2026-08-29, later — the figures got fixed and the card still contradicted itself.** With `totalOrdered` landed, Anneliese's card reads correctly; Marguerite's read **Orders 3 / $582.60** over three rows of $234.60, $276.00 and a cancelled $126.30, coming to $636.90. The rollup counts non-cancelled orders and the list did not, and its three-row window then dropped the ONE order she had been paid for — a card stating $72.00 collected, showing nothing that could account for it. The list now asks for the same population the figures were computed from, off one shared constant; the heading says when it is a window rather than the whole; and a partially refunded row says what went back, which nothing did before because only a FULL refund moves the status enough to earn a badge ([332](issues/332-her-customer-card-counted-three-orders-and-listed-a-different-three.md), fixed). Ease 8, unchanged: nothing about reaching or reading it moved. Not re-scored on quality either — the card is now arithmetically honest, and “Refunded” is still a grey badge. | P02 · P03 |
| Customers              | `crm.customers.list`       | 7      | 4 → 7 | Scored again by P03 with real money on the shop. The table is clean and holds up narrow, and every figure in the Total spent column was wrong: **-$42.00** on a customer who had paid $170 and been given $42 back, **$0.00** on one who had paid $147 in full, and the face value of an unpaid order on a third ([232](issues/232-jo-kim-paid-147-dollars-and-her-record-said-zero.md)). Ease is 4 because the one column she opens this screen for could not be trusted. Fixed in the write path; the drifted rows await their migration. That P02 note — “everyone is a ‘Lead’ including three clients with appointments this week” — stood for two personas as an observation and turned out to be a defect: a sale rung up at the till never advanced the buyer, so the one man who had put money in Devi’s hand across a counter was the only buyer filed as a stranger, while two who had paid nothing were customers ([280](issues/280-the-man-who-paid-her-at-the-counter-was-filed-as-a-stranger.md)). The stage is derived from the orders now, the same way the money is. Not re-scored: this pass looked at it in dark only. The footer told her phone about shift-click ([138](issues/138-eighty-seven-lists-each-wrote-their-own-instructions-for-a-keyboard.md)) — fixed. **2026-08-29, P03 — the default sort opened on the wrong people.** Taking the run-wide speed-at-volume record: the list paints instantly at 34 rows, and it was sorted by **Recent order** with every buyer BELOW every lead who had never ordered, because Postgres sorts `DESC` nulls-first. Ravi Naidoo, the only buyer on the Archive site, was row 30 of 30. The same line silently emptied the win-back tool, which asked for a page of that ordering and then discarded all of it ([322](issues/322-her-only-buyers-were-at-the-bottom-of-a-list-sorted-by-recent-order.md), fixed). Ease 4 → 7: the column she opens this screen for is trustworthy again and the list now opens on the people who have paid her. Held at 7 rather than higher because the drifted `total_spent` rows still await their migration, so three of her six buyers read $0.00 here. **Later that day — re-driven after the migration.** The list opens (it had begun throwing on its own default view, [331]) and now carries **Orders come to** beside **Paid you**: sorting by it puts Marguerite ($582.60) and Anneliese ($332.00) at the top instead of the bottom. The `$0.00` rows named above are gone — they were never drift, they were a shop taking manual payment being measured by what had cleared.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | P02 · P03 |

| Segment                | `crm.segment.detail`       | 8      | 7     | The rule builder is the best thing on this surface: plain-language fields and operators ("Days since last order is at most 90"), a live count in the bar as you type, a warning that names the field you have not filled in, and it refuses to preview rather than guessing — "Finish the rules to preview". What it could not do was FILL the group it had just counted: the bar said 2 of 29 match and the panel below said Members: 0, under its own promise to refresh on save ([234](issues/234-every-group-of-customers-was-empty-and-the-bridge-said-nobody-wanted-these.md)). Fixed; both numbers now agree and the members are named. Migration 20270418000000 has since landed and the bar now reads 4 of 29 match over Members: 4, naming all four. Gap to 10: the count is only ever as true as the rollup columns it reads, and nothing on this screen says when those were last agreed with the orders. | Groups of customers    | `crm.segments.list`        | 6 → 9  | 3 → 8 | Nine groups, and the two columns that carry the screen were both saying nothing true. **People** read "No members yet" on every row of a business with twenty-nine customers, because no group had ever been filled ([234](issues/234-every-group-of-customers-was-empty-and-the-bridge-said-nobody-wanted-these.md), [235](issues/235-she-imported-twenty-five-people-and-they-joined-nothing.md)); **Rules** read "From activity" on every row, for every tenant, forever, because the counter looked for four key names the stored tree does not have ([237](issues/237-nine-groups-and-the-same-three-words-beside-every-one.md)). Between them they hid a built-in whose rule contradicted its own description ([236](issues/236-new-customers-meant-people-who-had-bought-recently.md)). All fixed: nine rows now carry nine different sentences and real counts. Ease 3 because she could not tell what any group was, nor trust that any of them had anybody in it. The last gap, no way to recompute from the LIST, is now closed: **Update all** re-cuts every group in one press ([239](issues/239-eight-groups-were-out-of-date-and-the-only-fix-was-one-at-a-time.md)), and it is what surfaced [240](issues/240-she-imported-her-mailing-list-and-the-mailing-list-group-stayed-empty.md) — an import could not fill a group at all, because the evaluator runs in a different process. Gap to 10: a stale group still looks identical to an accurate one, so nothing tells her WHEN a count was last worked out. Fixed. Still cannot say a charge repeats ([121](issues/121-rent-is-due-every-month-and-the-invoice-can-only-be-raised-once.md)). **2026-09-07, P03 -- the first time anyone pressed Send.** The confirm read `billTo.email` alone, blank on most invoices, so it announced **there is no email address on this invoice yet** about one whose customer has one, then offered a Send it button that works -- the server falls back to the customer and the screen did not know ([439](issues/439-the-send-button-said-there-was-no-address-and-sent-it-anyway.md), fixed: the server now returns the resolved address). Everything else on the pane held: Send is correctly disabled while unsaved, the due-date helper changes its sentence once a date is set, and recording payment moved the linked ORDER to paid. **2026-09-07, act 105 -- the money did not add up.** Billing an order with a delivery charge put four figures on one card that could not all be true: Total $58.00, Paid $40.00, Amount due $27.00, and a **Not saved yet** warning about a document nobody had touched. The browser mirror of the server totals stopped at tax, and its own header named shipping and surcharge as part of the rule it mirrors; there was no Delivery row anywhere in the surface ([442](issues/442-the-delivery-charge-vanishes-from-the-bill-and-the-total-does-not-add-up.md), fixed). Down to 7 and back to 8: a totals card that disagrees with itself is worse than a missing one, and the false warning was training her to ignore the only guard against emailing a stale invoice. The due-date field also stopped saying **no deadline** on every retail invoice -- sending one now dates it. Holds at 8 -- the tax box is still asked for as a bare number beside a total that already knows the answer. | 2       |

The receivables band that answers _how much am I owed and how much of it is late_ was written, commented, careful -- it reads the aging report over ALL open documents rather than summing the page, so it cannot under-report past fifty -- and **nothing had ever imported it**; the list even carried a note saying so. Mounted in both consoles, with Refresh now invalidating the aging query as that note demanded. Mounting it alone would have made it lie: no retail invoice had ever carried a deadline, so **Late** could only ever read None. Both halves fixed together; proved by moving one deadline back a week and watching the row, the badge, the band and the Late filter all fire for the first time. ## Not in the console, and rated anyway

The console is not the whole product. These are scored on the same two axes by
whichever persona goes through them, because a business owner does not know where
one app stops and the next begins.

**The twelve published sites are scored as sites** — would a stranger buy from,
book on, or read this one without knowing it was a test (RULE #8)? Score the site
whole, and name its weakest page in the gap column, because that is the page a
real visitor lands on. Their design is judged as **the tenant's brand**, not
against sparx's restraint rules, which do not apply to a customer's website.

| P03 site — Juniper Row                      | 5 → 8  | 5 → 8 | Twenty-three pages walked as a stranger. **The type carries it**: one serif display face, a real measure, and her amber `#c77618` doing the work on every button and link. It holds at 390px with no sideways scroll on any page, and the words are the best thing on it — the size guide answers "between two sizes" before it is asked, Shipping and returns states the $9 plainly, and Contact promises a same-day reply from the one person who would send it. **Both scores were capped by the same thing, and it was the pictures.** Her shop front sold a $58 "square of silk twill, hand-rolled at the edges" over a photograph of a hank of knitting wool; her Collections page was seven grey placeholder tiles; and "Caring for knitwear so it lasts" was illustrated with hands crumpling paper towels. Four of the seven groups were also EMPTY — seeded from a blueprint whose sample products she had since deleted, so a shopper opening The knitwear edit on a shop that sells a knit was told "Nothing in this collection yet." All fixed as her: a real photograph on every product and every group, her own products in every group, and [338] so the description she writes for a photo is read on the CARD and not only on the product page. **Two of the six gaps are now closed at the platform.** [339] fixed the journal's 128px step — `articleBody()` was narrowing the BAND rather than capping the measure on its content, which is what the rest of that file already did; her blog page stores no tree, so the factory fix reaches her live posts. [340] fixed the reach rule that should have caught the unlinked /collections and did not: it borrowed `BUILTIN_PATHS` (the addresses that EXIST) to answer whether anything REACHES one, exempting all three seeded browse indexes. Her pre-publish check now reports it in her own words, and new sites carry the link in the footer. **Gap to 10, what remains.** (1) Alignment has no rule ACROSS the starter set, and the worst instance of it is now closed. Measured on her About page: the footer's columns started at 703px and her words at **943px**, because that page was the only one on the site set to `max-w-2xl` where four others use `max-w-6xl` — 240px of disagreement with her own header and footer. Fixed on her page (band at the site's measure, prose held at `max-w-2xl` inside it, the structure her own Made in the studio page already used) AND at the platform, because the reason she could never have found it herself was [348]: the control that sets the width showed six plain buttons with nothing marked whenever the value came from a smaller size, which is nearly always. What is still open is the CONVENTION — the starter's bands run `max-w-xl` through `max-w-6xl` with nothing choosing between them, and that is a design decision for the starter set rather than a bug fix. (2) — closed: About was two paragraphs and no photograph on a site whose entire argument is that one person sews the clothes. Rebuilt as her: 1,550 bytes to 10,047, one section to four, no pictures to three. **The studio on Larimer Street** with a photograph of her folded cloth and a real link into How it's made; **There are two of us** naming her and Ines with the work photographs, truthful alt text, and the sample third person deleted; **Where to next** carrying three live links. Opening it as her is also what turned up [346], [347] and [349] — the studio announcing her shop as "Built for the work" for a beat on every page open, Insert burying every group written in her language behind 118 rows of Container and Overflow List and App Shell, and the canvas rendering `src=""` while refusing a bound product photo because `img` is a void tag. (3) — closed: Collections AND Categories are now linked from her footer, added as her through the very remedy the finding prints; her live Explore column reads Shop · Collections · Categories · How it's made · Journal · About · Contact · Search · Size guide · Shipping and returns, and her pre-publish check went 16 → 14. **New this pass, from Brandon's correction that the browse pages are three different jobs rather than duplicates:** her shop had filters and NO WAY TO SEARCH IT on any surface, now fixed ([341]); her Size filter ran S, M, L, XS, XL although she declared the right order ([342], **fixed** — a public `option-axes` read now carries her declared ladder to all four browse surfaces, merged across products topologically because a position only means something inside the product that set it; her Knitwear page reads XS, S, M, L, XL); and `/category` cold-loaded in another company's brand primary rather than her amber ([343], **fixed** — and it was two causes: a failed theme fetch was indistinguishable from having no theme, AND the theme it fell back to was one product's flagship look on a renderer that serves both brands. The base is silicaui's own neutral now, a failed read is retried and then logged, and a live un-themed Piggles shop contains the other brand's hex zero times where it used to carry it on every page). (4) — closed: the product page's hero photograph was `loading="lazy"`, so the largest thing above the fold was the last thing requested ([345], fixed). silicaui's `Image` atom ignores a `loading` prop entirely, so both LCP heroes are raw `img` now while every card stays lazy; her journal post took the fix immediately and the stored product tree is repaired by a heal whose recognizer was measured across all 13 stored trees before it was trusted. (5) — closed at the platform: the studio address and Thursday hours on Contact were set at 14px, in the `caption()` slot the enquiry section reserves for "or call us". A fair size for a phone number and not for the only address on the site, and the slot is the OTHER WAY TO REACH THE BUSINESS whatever an owner writes in it ([344], fixed — with seven more of the same shape across the kit: delivery cost, what a price includes, "call ahead", "Outside these? Call us", an allergy instruction). Her own Contact page is a stored tree and a cohort of ONE (1 page in 419), so it was fixed by hand rather than by fleet repair code — and the issue's claim that she could not have done that herself was wrong. The Design panel's **Text → Size** row rides exactly the `text-sm` / `text-base` ladder, so the repair was one click, keeping her heading, her paragraph and her sentence. It had to be made at the PHONE size: on desktop the row read “Small — from a smaller size”, and clicking there would have left every phone visitor on 14px. Reading that off the chips is [348] working an hour after it shipped. Live at **16px**, matching the paragraph above it. **Then her Contact FORM was tested rather than looked at, and it was a black hole.** A sizing question sent through it as a shopper reached nothing: zero network calls from a clean load, `data-sui-state=“success”`, the text still in the boxes, and `form_submissions` holding three rows that belong to another tenant. The shelf's shared `form()` helper shipped the host ref `'submit'`, which the storefront routes nowhere, and an unrecognised ref is an error at no layer ([350]) — so every form on every tenant site swallowed every enquiry and thanked the sender. Separately the visitor was told nothing either way, the behavior's default confirmation being a 1x1px clipped live region ([351]). And repairing the 29 stored pages found that `upgradePageBody` **was called by nothing at all**, which had also silently voided [345]'s hero repair ([352]). All three fixed; **the end-to-end proof on her live site is still owed** — api-rest was down when the work finished, so her stored page still carries the dead ref and no message has yet been watched landing in her inbox. What is otherwise left in this row is (1)'s convention, which is a design call. **2026-09-01, the shop walked as a customer, and the two biggest finds of the whole run are here.** [371]: **the Quantity box in every buy box was frozen at 1** — typing, the spinner arrows and the up-arrow key all did nothing, so nobody could buy two of anything on any shop on the platform. HTML's `value` (where a control starts) walked into React's `value` (what it is pinned to), and a pinned field with no `onChange` never moves. The older renderer already handled it with a comment and a test; the newer silica walk inherited neither, and `wizeworks/apps/site` was the one app in the repo with no test seat. Fixed, seat added, 19 tests. Confirmed by buying three. [370]: her **Last chance** shelf — the only rule-driven one — was empty while her console said a size had run out, through four faults ending in the indexer skipping every variant-keyed event because it read `productId` off payloads that carry only `variantId`. Fixed; the shelf shows the product. **Otherwise the site holds up well.** All 21 footer links resolve and all six legal pages carry 2,300 to 2,600 words; Home, Shop and a product page have no sideways scroll at 360px and the mobile drawer carries the full nav; a keyboard-only purchase completes with the focus ring visible throughout; her structured data emits Organization and WebSite with a SearchAction; and the footer's facts match her Contact page. Her own writing remains the best thing on it — the made-to-order notice on the Marlow Knit states the ready date, the days needed, and that no card is charged. New gap: [373] five of her titles print the business name twice, because the SEO preview did not show the suffix the site adds; and [375] three of her legal pages still carry the starter's invented numbers, one of which contradicts her own shipping page. **2026-09-01, the site's own search — [378].** A customer typing _returns_ into her search box was told **"No results for 'returns'"** and offered **Browse all products**, on a site whose footer links a Return Policy, a Returns page and a Shipping and returns page; _privacy_, _knitwear_ and _fabric_ the same. Products were found perfectly, so nothing looked broken. The `entities` index held 30 documents platform-wide and **not one was a page or an article**: the `cms_page` projector read the deprecated `Page` model, which has zero rows on the whole database, and articles indexed as `cms_entry`, which the public type list did not include. The strip to show them was already built and already called. Fixed at both ends, plus the page then telling the shopper two opposite things at once. Now _knitwear_ returns her collection, her article and the Marlow Knit, and _returns_ returns her Return Policy. **Builder pages are still in no index** — searching _Larimer_, her studio address on About and Contact, still finds nothing, and that is the larger half of the same shape. **The account area, walked as her customer.** All nine sub-pages load, Orders lists four with semantic status badges, and Returns shows an approved return with a plain instruction. One layout fault, measured rather than eyeballed: the customer's own email address was painted **11px over** the sentence in the next column — 267px of text in a 196px box, because an email has no space to wrap at and the sidebar fits about 22 characters, so it hit most real addresses rather than long ones ([379], fixed with `break-all` + `min-w-0`, not truncation). The size guide, About and How it's made are the best writing on the site, and all six pages hold at 360px with no sideways scroll. | P03     |

| P03 — the shopper's account, after the sale | 5 → 8  | 3 → 8 | Design: the order page was already the good part — a real status timeline, the carrier and a live tracking link, the address, the totals. It lost three black rules across the status card ([293]) and a list that rendered as a centered stack ([294]), and gained a refund line that tells her what she actually paid ([292]). **Ease moved twice.** The header now knows her ([291]) instead of offering to sign in a signed-in customer, and — the big one — **she can send something back herself** ([297]): pick the lines, say why, ask for money or a swap, and follow it, on a business where returns are 22% of orders. What is left: the orders list still names an order by number, date and total only, so finding the right one among many means opening each. **Re-scored on 2026-08-28**, and the ceiling on both was money: her order page showed a price nobody had quoted her ([298]) until the discount reached the order, and it now names what came off each item the way the console does. On a phone the whole area opened on a 635px menu with her order below it ([299]) — 359px now. Held at 356px with no horizontal overflow. What is left is unchanged: the orders list still names an order by number, date and total only. | P03 — Cart → Checkout, as the shopper       | 6 → 8  | 4 → 8 | The three steps read well and the copy is honestly good — "Once we know where" for a shipping line it cannot know yet, "Placing this order does not take any money now", the made-to-order date carried the whole way. Both scores were capped by the same thing: **the money on screen was not the money written down.** The button said $129.20 and the order said $152.00 ([298]); an ended sale went on being honored right through it ([300]); a code typed after checkout began never counted, and one step showed the saving while the next did not ([301]). All three fixed, and the button's own total is now sent back so nothing is written for a figure she was not shown. Gap to 10: the review page never re-reads, so the label can sit stale until she presses it — the press is caught and refused, but she finds out at the button rather than before it. ## How this list was built

```
node piggles/scripts/gen-pane-ratings.mjs
```

Generated rather than typed, from three sources — because a pane is only what a
person can actually open and read:

| Source                      | Gives                                                       |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lib/surfaces/catalog/*.ts` | every registered surface                                    |
| `lib/console/vocabulary.ts` | what Piggles **calls** it — 99 of the 323 are renamed there |
| `lib/console/product.tsx`   | `hiddenSurfaces`, which are not Piggles panes at all        |

Grouped by app through `modules` and `claims` in `packages/config/src/apps.ts`,
so Partners shows the supplier screens it claims from Stock.

**The names here are the ones on screen, not the catalog's.** sparx calls
`commerce.carts.list` "Carts"; a Piggles owner reads "Baskets left behind", and
rating a screen means rating the words on it.

**Regenerate when the catalog changes** — before a run, never during one. A pane
added after this file was written is a pane nobody is asked to rate, and a
missing row reads as a covered one. The rubric above the marker survives a
regeneration; scores inside the generated block do not.
